texts.li: [theirLowtech] Settlers of {FACTION} have founded a new town, {PLACE}, {TALE}. The first houses are up and the well is dug, and they held their first market before the roofs were on.\n\nThey are short of nearly everything, timber most of all, and they will be looking for neighbors to trade with.

[theirHightech] {FACTION} have put a new settlement on the map: {PLACE}, {TALE}. The first prefab walls went up last week, and someone has already painted the name over the gate, slightly crooked.\n\nA new town needs everything at once, and {PLACE} will be looking for neighbors to trade with.

[spring] With the snow gone, settlers of {FACTION} have walked out to found a new town, {PLACE}, {TALE}. They are mostly young, mostly hopeful, and mostly short of everything.\n\nTheir first letter to the colony is already on the road.

summaries.li: {PLACE} is on the map to stay. Its first traders will come by soon, and caravans and visitors from {FACTION} come more often while the town finds its feet.

texts.li: The settlers of {PLACE} have sent a runner to ask whether they may count the colony among their friends. A neighbor's gift is the custom at a time like this, and it's remembered.\n\nThey are short of timber too, and would pay a fair price for some.

li.label: Send a gift ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The runner takes the silver back to {PLACE}, where the settlers mean to spend it on a bell for the meeting hall.
li.deed: sent a gift to the settlers of {PLACE}

li.label: Sell them timber (100 wood)
li.outcome: Carters from {PLACE} come for the logs with an empty wagon, and pay more than the going price, since they need them now.

li.label: Wish them well
li.outcome: The runner goes home with the colony's good wishes and an empty purse.

texts.li: [gift,!timber] {PLACE} has found its feet. The fields are marked out, the walls are up, and the bell bought with the colony's silver rings for market every week.
[timber] {PLACE} has found its feet. There are colony timbers in half the roofs there, and the settlers say so when they come by to trade.
[!gift,!timber] {PLACE} has found its feet: walls up, fields marked out, a market on the first day of every week. The colony has new neighbors, for better or worse.

[drought] {PLACE}, {TALE}, is being abandoned. Its wells have been going dry for two years, and this year the last one failed.\n\n{FACTION} are moving everyone to {ITEM}. The road past the colony is full of carts, and not everyone on it has somewhere to go.

[raids] {PLACE}, {TALE}, has been raided so often that {FACTION} have stopped rebuilding it. The order has gone out to leave.\n\nThe road to {ITEM} is full of carts. Some of the people on it would rather go anywhere else.

[sickness] A fever went through {PLACE}, {TALE}, last season, and the people who lived through it don't want to stay where it happened. {FACTION} are giving the town up.\n\nMost are headed for {ITEM}. Some aren't sure where they're headed at all.

[mine] The mine that {PLACE} was built around has given out. {FACTION} are giving up the town, {TALE}, and moving its people to {ITEM}.\n\nMiners are not, as a rule, good at sitting still. Some of them will come this way looking for work.

[river] The river that {PLACE} was built on has moved its bed, and left the town's mills standing over dry stones. {FACTION} are giving it up.\n\nThe road from {PLACE}, {TALE}, to {ITEM} is busy with carts, and some of them will come this way.

summaries.li: When it's over, {PLACE} will be gone from the map. Until then, people leaving it may ask the colony for shelter, and what they leave behind is anyone's to take.

texts.li: A family from {PLACE} has stopped at the colony's gate instead of going on to {ITEM}. They have a barrow of bedding, a dog and a lot of questions about the colony.\n\nThey'd like to stay. They've heard it's a good place.
[raids] A family from {PLACE} has turned up at the gate. They've been raided twice in a year and don't trust {ITEM} to be any safer.\n\nThey ask whether the colony would take them in.

li.label: Take them in
li.outcome: The family unloads the barrow. The dog has already found the warmest spot.

li.label: Feed them and send them on
li.outcome: They eat, sleep a night and go on toward {ITEM} in the morning.

li.label: Point them to {ITEM}
li.outcome: The family is pointed down the road to {ITEM}, and goes.

texts.li: The last carts are leaving {PLACE}, and what didn't fit is being left behind: timber, tools, half a mill. {FACTION} don't much mind who takes the rest.\n\n{A_nameDef} says the colony could fill a few carts of its own. Some think it's no different from picking over a grave.

li.label: Salvage what's left
li.outcome: The colony's carts come back loaded with what {PLACE} left behind.

li.label: Leave it
li.outcome: The colony leaves {PLACE} alone. Somebody else will take it.

texts.li: The last of {FACTION} left {PLACE} three days ago. The gates stand open, the roofs are already going, and grass is creeping in at the edges of the road.\n\nIn a year it will be a ruin, and in ten a story.
[salvaged] {PLACE} is empty. What the colony carted away is in its stores now, and the rest is the weather's business.\n\nSwallows have moved into the old mill.
{PLACE} is mostly empty now, but not all of it. A few families refused to leave, and {FACTION} have stopped trying to make them. The town stays on the map, smaller and quieter than it was.

[theirLowtech] The roads through the region are safe this year, or safe enough, and the merchants have come out in force. Every inn between {PLACE} and the colony is full, and {FACTION}'s caravan masters are drawing new routes on the tables in spilled beer.\n\nWhile it lasts, the colony's goods are worth more to more people.

[theirHightech] Fuel is cheap and the roads are clear, and every trading house in the region knows it. {FACTION} have put three new caravans on the road out of {PLACE} this month alone.\n\nIt won't last. Everyone on the road knows that too, which is why they're all in such a hurry.

[summer] Long days and dry roads have brought the merchants out early this year. Caravans of {FACTION} and everyone else are passing the colony every few days, and the talk in {PLACE} is of nothing but prices.

summaries.li: Trader caravans and merchants with offers come much more often. Anyone with goods to sell will find buyers.

texts.li: Merchants have started cutting across the colony's land to save half a day on the road to {PLACE}. They are polite about it. They also leave gates open and drink from the well.\n\nSome at the colony think the merchants should pay for the privilege; a toll would bring in about {COUNT} silver. Others think a rest stop with water and a fire would make friends of every trader in the region.

li.label: Charge a toll
li.outcome: A rope goes across the track, and a jar goes beside it. The merchants pay, and grumble about it in every town they visit.

li.label: Set up a rest stop (60 wood)
li.outcome: A shelter goes up by the track, with a fire pit and a trough. The merchants notice.

li.label: the wood for the rest stop

li.deed: kept a rest stop for traders

li.label: Leave it
li.outcome: The merchants keep cutting across. Somebody puts a sign on the well asking them to close the gate.

texts.li: [toll] The trading season is winding down, and the caravans are going home. The colony's toll jar did well. The merchants have been telling every town on the road about it, and not kindly.
[reststop] The trading season is winding down. The merchants who warmed themselves at the colony's fire will be back next year, and they will bring friends.
[!toll,!reststop] The trading season is winding down, and the caravans are going home with lighter wagons and heavier purses. The roads will be quieter for a while.

li.chronicle: A busy trading season came to an end.

texts.li: {FACTION} are holding {NAME} at {PLACE}, the biggest in years. Traders, players, cooks and craftsmen are coming from every town in the region, and there will be contests on the green: the best shot, the best cook, the finest work.\n\nThe colony has been invited, along with everyone else.

[theirHightech] {FACTION} have announced {NAME} at {PLACE}: market stalls, music, a contest in every trade worth having, and floodlights so it can run all night.\n\nThe colony has been invited, along with everyone else in the region.

summaries.li: The colony can send a cart of its surplus to sell at fair prices, and put its best forward in a contest. Visitors and traders come more often while it lasts.

texts.li: {FACTION} have offered the colony a stall at {NAME}. The colony has {COUNT} {THING} it doesn't need, and fair prices are better than any trader's.\n\nThe fair's carts are going around the villages for stall goods, and would bring the takings back when the fair closes.

li.label: Send the cart ({COUNT} {THING})
li.outcome: The {THING} goes onto one of the fair's carts, bound for {PLACE}. The takings will come back the same way when the fair closes.

li.label: Not this year
li.outcome: The colony keeps its goods at home.

texts.li: There is a contest in {SKILL} at {NAME}, with a prize for the winner and bragging rights for the winner's town. {A_nameDef} is the best the colony has, and the others have been dropping hints all week.

li.label: Put {A_nameDef}'s name down
li.outcome: {A_nameDef}'s name goes on the list. The colony will hear how it went when the fair closes.

li.label: Not this time
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} stays out of it this year.

texts.li: [sent,prize] {NAME} has closed, and it went well for the colony. The fair's carter brought back the takings, {COUNT} silver for the colony's goods, and {B_nameDef} won the contest in {SKILL} and brought the prize home.\n\nThe colony's name was on a lot of lips at {PLACE} this week.

[sent,noPrize] {NAME} has closed. The colony's takings came back with the fair's carter, {COUNT} silver for its goods.\n\n{B_nameDef} did well in the contest in {SKILL}, but not well enough. Next year, {B_nameDef} says.
[sent,!entered] {NAME} has closed, and the fair's carter has been around with the colony's takings: {COUNT} silver, in a sealed bag.
[!sent,prize] {NAME} has closed, and {B_nameDef} won the contest in {SKILL}. The prize came home with the news, and so did the bragging.
[!sent,noPrize] {NAME} has closed. {B_nameDef} came close in the contest in {SKILL}, and has been explaining the judges' mistake to anyone who will listen.
[!sent,!entered] {NAME} has closed, and the travelers who went to it are drifting home with stories. The colony will hear them for weeks.

Once in a generation, the faithful of {FACTION} walk to the old shrine at {PLACE}, and this is that year. They are on every road, in twos and threes and in long singing columns, and many of them pass the colony.\n\nMost carry little and ask for less. All of them will remember where they were welcomed.

[theirHightech] Some walk and some ride in the backs of trucks, and all of them are singing. The faithful of {FACTION} are on their way to the old shrine at {PLACE}, as they are once in a generation, and the colony sits on one of their roads.\n\nMost carry little and ask for less. All of them will remember where they were welcomed.

[colony:Devout] The faithful of {FACTION} are walking to the old shrine at {PLACE} this year, as they do once in a generation, and the talk on the roads is that the colony keeps its own faith well. More than a few of them mean to stop there on the way.\n\nMost carry little, and will ask for less.

summaries.li: Pilgrims and travelers pass the colony far more often, hungry ones among them. Hosting them costs food and earns lasting goodwill with {FACTION}.

texts.li: A long column of pilgrims has stopped at the edge of the colony's land. Their leader asks whether they may camp by the water for a few nights and rest their feet before the last stretch to {PLACE}. They would need feeding, {COUNT} portions or so.\n\nThey have nothing to trade but songs and news. Some at the colony think they should pay to camp; most think that would be a shameful thing to ask of pilgrims.

li.label: Welcome them ({COUNT} food)
li.outcome: The pilgrims camp by the water for three nights. The singing carries all the way to the colony after dark.
li.deed: hosted pilgrims on the road to {PLACE}

li.label: Let them camp, for a fee (60 silver)
li.outcome: The pilgrims pass a bowl among themselves until the fee is in it, and camp by the water. They sing less than they might have.

li.label: Ask them to move on
li.outcome: The pilgrims pack up without complaint and walk on to find another place to rest.

texts.li: On their way home from {PLACE}, the pilgrims stopped again at the colony's gate. Their leader said a blessing over the fields and the people in them, in the old way, and they were gone before anyone could offer supper.\n\nEven the colony's doubters kept their heads bowed until it was over.

[hosted] The last of the pilgrims have passed on their way home from {PLACE}. A few of them left something at the gate as they went: small things from the shrine, and some that aren't so small.\n\n{FACTION} will hear about the colony's welcome from every one of them.
[fee] The last of the pilgrims have passed on their way home from {PLACE}. They paid what the colony asked, and in {FACTION}'s halls they will say so.
[!hosted,!fee] The roads are quiet again. The pilgrimage to {PLACE} is over for another generation.

Someone in {PLACE} found silver in a creek bed last month, and now half the region is out with picks and pans. Prospectors have been passing the colony for days, and some of them are looking hard at the colony's own hills.\n\nMost will find nothing. A few will get rich, and a few will want to stay.

[theirHightech] A survey crew out of {PLACE} hit a silver seam last month, and the news got out before the claim was filed. Now prospectors with metal detectors and borrowed trucks are combing every hill in the region, the colony's included.\n\nThe claims office at {PLACE} has a line out the door and around the block.

summaries.li: Travelers and prospectors pass the colony often, and some will ask to stay. The colony can let them work its land for a share of what they find.

texts.li: A party of prospectors from {PLACE} has asked to work the creek beds on the colony's land. They will pay a share of whatever they find when they leave, or {COUNT} silver now, whichever the colony prefers.\n\nThey seem honest enough. Prospectors usually do.

li.label: Let them dig, for a share
li.outcome: The prospectors stake out the creek beds. The colony's share will come when they're done, if there's anything to share.
li.deed: let prospectors work its land for a share

li.label: Let them dig, for {COUNT} silver now
li.outcome: The prospectors pay up front and stake out the creek beds. Whatever they find is theirs.
li.deed: sold prospectors the right to dig

li.label: Keep them off the land
li.outcome: The prospectors are told the colony's land is not for digging. They go and dig somebody else's.

texts.li: Somebody at the prospectors' camp found a nugget the size of a thumb in the colony's creek. Since then the lamps down there have burned all night.

One of the prospectors has given up on getting rich. After three weeks in the creek beds with nothing to show for it, there are worse things than a roof, regular meals and work that pays in something besides hope.\n\nThe prospector asks whether the colony could use another pair of hands.

li.label: Take them in
li.outcome: The prospector hangs up the pan for good and moves in.
li.deed: took in a prospector who gave up

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: The prospector shrugs, picks up the pan again and heads for the next hill.

texts.li: [share] The rush has moved on to the next valley. The prospectors who worked the colony's creeks left the colony's share at the gate on their way out: {COUNT} silver, counted twice in front of witnesses.
[fee] The rush has moved on to the next valley, and the prospectors with it. The colony was paid up front. Whether they found more than that, they didn't say.
[!share,!fee] The rush has moved on to the next valley. The colony's hills are quiet again, and still full of whatever was or wasn't in them.
